problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-5x{y}^{′}+12y=0,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-5x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+12{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-5\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+12{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-5\lambda +12] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-5\lambda +12 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +12 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We solve the auxiliary equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +12 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +9)-9+12 & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)^{2} & =-3 \\ \lambda -3 & =\pm \sqrt{3}\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =3\pm \sqrt{3}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =3\pm \sqrt{3}\text{i}.$

Now, we note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3+\sqrt{3}\text{i}} & ={x}^{3}{e}^{\text{i}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}={x}^{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)) \\ {x}^{3-\sqrt{3}\text{i}} & ={x}^{3}{e}^{-\text{i}\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}={x}^{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(x) & =A{x}^{3+\sqrt{3}\text{i}}+B{x}^{3-\sqrt{3}\text{i}} \\  & =A{x}^{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x))+B{x}^{3}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)) \\  & =(A+B){x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\text{i}(A-B){x}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can rewrite $y(x)$ as

$$
y(x)={x}^{3}({c}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+{c}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x))
$$

where ${c}_{1}=A+B$ and ${c}_{2}=\text{i}(A-B).$
